checkpoints.description: [1/5] Renderer core: VT100 terminal layer, char-cell screen buffer with depth, low-poly 3D mesh-to-ASCII sprite baker with directional lighting, value-noise heightmap terrain

impact_assessment.why: User wants a 2.5D medieval RPG whose ASCII cells are so small and dense they read as pixels, showing near-real models: needs a from-scratch stdlib-only renderer, not a curses demo
impact_assessment.benefits: A dependency-free, portable ASCII 3D engine and a playable RPG demonstrating it; every subsystem unit-testable without a TTY
impact_assessment.risks: contract: renderer APIs (buffer/mesh/atlas) must stay stable while gameplay layers build on them; dependency: none beyond Python 3.10 stdlib, no numpy/curses; concurrency: single-threaded game loop, non-blocking input only, no sleeps in tests; state: save files and sprite caches must be atomic and seed-deterministic
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep renderer/gameplay boundaries as small frozen dataclasses and pure functions; fixed seed world gen; headless --demo and render-to-text verification baked into tests; all file writes via temp+replace

checkpoints.description: [2/5] World simulation: entities with AI FSMs, spatial props, combat resolution, quests, dialogue, shops, save/load
[3/5] RPG systems: items/inventory/equipment, XP levels, enemy drops, shrine healing, captain quest chain
[4/5] Shell: HUD/minimap/menus, game states, camera, demo and benchmark modes, CLI with error triads
[5/5] Verification: 51/51 tests pass, aikit check 4/4 gates (test, hygiene, guidelines, secrets), demo/benchmark/screenshot smoke-exit 0; checklists: passed

[1/1] Code review fixes: water fog scale, pack_rgb clamp, gold pickup list mutation, HUD bar overlap, dead game-state wiring, min terminal width; 6 failing-first regression tests added; checklists: passed
